title: Welcome / server entry
goal: Connect to the family server or try the app.
usability: The short form is easy to scan. It assumes that a family member knows what a server URL means.
interaction: Connect remains disabled until the field has text. The URL keyboard suits the field.
primary: Connect is available, but the help for obtaining an address deserves a clearer position.
apple: The native form and controls fit iOS. The first screen needs a clearer household purpose.
change: Explain the family benefit. Ask the user to obtain the address from their family admin. Keep Try Demo secondary.

title: Setup help
goal: Understand how to join a family or set up a server.
usability: The help starts with Docker, OIDC, PKCE, and environment variables. This suits a server admin, but burdens family members.
interaction: Done provides a clear exit. The repository link provides full instructions.
primary: A family member needs the server address and an account before deployment instructions.
apple: The sheet is native. Progressive disclosure better separates common and advanced help.
change: Lead with three join steps. Keep server deployment in an admin section and retain the full guide.

title: Invalid server address
goal: Correct an invalid connection address.
usability: The form keeps the address and shows an inline error. This supports recovery.
interaction: The user can edit and retry. Avoid dismissing the keyboard or replacing the whole form.
primary: The error needs to identify the required address format next to the field.
apple: Inline feedback and native text entry fit the platform.
change: Keep the error beside a persistent label. Use a specific correction and retain the entered value.

title: Today
goal: Know what needs attention now and complete household work.
usability: Agenda, meals, chores, and departures share the page. The current order puts meals before overdue chores and departures last.
interaction: Chore completion, the chore action menu, weather, events, and meals provide direct entry points.
primary: The meal plan takes priority over chores, as confirmed by the user. Keep meal actions above the chore list.
apple: Native navigation and grouped content suit iOS 26. Content priority needs more work than the materials.
change: Put a near departure first, then the meal plan, the agenda, and overdue and today’s chores. Keep weather compact and omit empty departure cards.

title: Weather detail
goal: Read local conditions and the forecast.
usability: The detail screen keeps weather out of Today. Each hourly row repeats the full date, which slows the scan.
interaction: The header weather control opens the detail screen. Back returns to Today.
primary: Current conditions, the forecast, and data freshness should appear in that order.
apple: Native navigation and semantic type provide a suitable base.
change: Keep the current conditions prominent. Use shorter hourly time labels. Retain all 24 hourly forecasts, weather advice, freshness, and Open-Meteo attribution.

title: Event detail
goal: Inspect an event and know when to leave.
usability: The title, date, location, description, and departure are present. Departure follows the description, which can push it down.
interaction: The event opens from Today or Calendar. The same detail should serve both routes.
primary: Group the start time, location, and departure before a long description.
apple: The native detail view fits iOS. Better grouping improves the reading order.
change: Put date and location together. Put the departure immediately below them. Keep the full description below.

title: Today chore menu
goal: Skip a particular task without changing its repeat rule.
usability: A menu keeps secondary actions away from the completion control. The affected chore needs clear context.
interaction: The ellipsis opens the menu. An outside tap dismisses the native popover when no Cancel control appears.
primary: Complete remains the direct action. Skip needs a short explanation of its effect.
apple: The native menu is appropriate. Do not replace it with a custom floating panel.
change: Include the chore name and assignee. Explain Skip. Add a route to the chore setup.

title: Calendar: month and zoom
goal: Browse dates and inspect the selected day.
usability: The grid provides useful month context. Narrow date columns truncate event titles even when the rows are tall.
interaction: Month scroll, pinch zoom, date selection, and Today work in the captured interaction tests.
primary: A readable selected-day list helps users inspect events without guessing a truncated title.
apple: The system toolbar and floating tab bar fit iOS 26. The content should remain the focus.
change: Keep the current Calendar design and interactions, as selected by the user. Only remove arrival-margin text. Earlier layout proposals are superseded.

title: Calendar: day and event overlap
goal: Inspect the daily schedule and open an event.
usability: The timeline communicates time and separates overlapping events. Text competes for width in simultaneous blocks.
interaction: Tapping an event opens details. Swipe changes the day. Today restores the current date.
primary: The date, all-day items, and full event names need to remain readable.
apple: The native toolbar and direct timeline navigation follow the platform. Avoid adding glass behind event content.
change: Keep the current Calendar design and interactions, as selected by the user. Only remove arrival-margin text. Earlier layout proposals are superseded.

title: Calendar: week
goal: Compare the schedule across seven days.
usability: The week capture shows event titles broken into one-letter lines in seven narrow columns. This prevents useful inspection.
interaction: The view menu selects Week. Select a day or event to inspect details.
primary: The overview needs a readable path to the full event name.
apple: A week overview is appropriate, but the phone width requires an inspection layer.
change: Keep the current Calendar design and interactions, as selected by the user. Only remove arrival-margin text. Earlier layout proposals are superseded.

title: Calendar: year
goal: Move to a month in another part of the year.
usability: The compact month grids suit broad date navigation. Keep selection obvious.
interaction: Year opens a month. Today restores the current period.
primary: The year and month entry points are the main information and actions.
apple: The year-to-month hierarchy matches familiar calendar navigation.
change: Keep the current Calendar design and interactions, as selected by the user. Only remove arrival-margin text. Earlier layout proposals are superseded.

title: Calendar: accessibility text
goal: Inspect the schedule with large text.
usability: The accessibility route uses an agenda and date picker instead of forcing large text into a month grid.
interaction: The date picker and view menu keep date navigation available.
primary: Full event labels and the selected date matter more than a dense overview.
apple: This is a good adaptive pattern. Preserve it when changing the standard calendar layout.
change: Keep the current Calendar design and interactions, as selected by the user. Only remove arrival-margin text. Earlier layout proposals are superseded.

title: Chore setup list
goal: Create and manage chore rules.
usability: The screen title says Chores while the tab says Tasks. At maximum text size, Show inactive chores consumes much of the first viewport.
interaction: Rows open setup details. The plus control creates a chore. Inactive chores can be shown.
primary: Creation and repeat rules are available. Users also need a direct route to chores due today.
apple: The list and toolbar are native. Consistent destination names improve wayfinding.
change: Rename the tab Chores. Move Show inactive below the active rules. Keep completion on Today and add a direct Today link.

title: Chore setup detail and history
goal: Inspect the repeat rule, current task, and history.
usability: The setup, current task, and history are clear groups. “Complete or skip this task on Home” names a destination that is actually Today.
interaction: Edit and delete are below the history. The completion instruction has no direct link.
primary: The current task deserves a higher position and a direct route to its action.
apple: Native list sections suit the detail. Place the frequent edit action in the toolbar.
change: Put the current task first. Replace Home with Today and make the instruction a link. Keep history and deletion.

title: New chore
goal: Create a chore and assign its schedule.
usability: The form includes the required capabilities, but it mixes details, rotating assignees, dates, and advanced repeat options in one long form.
interaction: Save stays in the toolbar. Selecting no assignees means everyone; the existing footer explains this.
primary: The name, first due date, and eligible people should lead. Advanced repeat settings can follow.
apple: The native form and sheet are suitable. Plain labels and progressive disclosure improve the interaction.
change: Use “Due date” and “Due time” labels. Show a repeat summary and keep advanced conditions in a repeat section.

title: Edit chore and repeat rule
goal: Change a chore rule without changing the outstanding task.
usability: The existing explanation preserves an important distinction: rule changes affect the next task.
interaction: The form retains current task ownership and dates. The weekday controls are compact for touch.
primary: Make the current task constraint and resulting repeat rule easy to read.
apple: The native form is appropriate. Aim for 44-point default touch targets on custom weekday controls.
change: Keep the current-task explanation. Use full-size weekday controls and a readable repeat summary.

title: Deletion confirmations
goal: Confirm a destructive change with enough context.
usability: The app uses native confirmation dialogs. Naming the item and the effect reduces mistakes.
interaction: Delete confirms the action. Cancel or an outside tap dismisses the dialog, depending on presentation.
primary: The user needs to know exactly what disappears and whether history remains.
apple: Native confirmation dialogs fit iOS 26. Preserve their system appearance and roles.
change: Name the item in the title. Explain the effect, including area contents or retained chore history.

title: Food / daily meal plan
goal: Read the selected day’s meals and reach recipes.
usability: The date strip and meal rows are clear. Large empty slots push Recipes down. At maximum text size, the header delays access to the first meal.
interaction: The planned meal row opens Edit. A separate View recipe action opens the recipe.
primary: Users often want to read or cook a planned recipe. Opening it should be the main planned-meal action.
apple: Native lists and date selection fit iOS. Keep navigation predictable across empty and planned meals.
change: Use the chosen Food overview with Meal plan and Recipes navigation rows, followed by today’s meals. Open each destination with a normal Back action.

title: Full week meal plan
goal: Plan meals across the Friday–Thursday week.
usability: The week keeps all three meal types for every day. Repeated empty-row helper text makes it long.
interaction: The selected week carries through from Food. Week navigation remains available.
primary: Keep the week range and day headings clear while reducing empty-slot height.
apple: The native list is suitable. Compact content improves scanning without removing meal slots.
change: Keep Friday–Thursday boundaries. Use shorter empty rows and retain all breakfast, lunch, and dinner actions.

title: Add meal / recipe selection
goal: Choose a recipe or enter a custom meal.
usability: One name field supports two paths. The footer explains Return, but the distinction between text and a linked recipe needs emphasis.
interaction: Typing filters recipes. Choosing a recipe retains its link. Return saves a custom name.
primary: Save and the selected recipe need an obvious state.
apple: Native sheet controls suit the task. Persistent labels help when the keyboard is open.
change: Keep Save visible. State “Choose a recipe or save the meal name.” Show a checkmark for the selected recipe.

title: Edit meal
goal: Change a planned meal without an unexpected recipe-link change.
usability: The existing editor supports both custom meals and linked recipes.
interaction: Changing a linked meal name removes the recipe link. That effect needs clear feedback.
primary: Show the linked recipe, Save, and Remove meal distinctly.
apple: Keep the native editor and recipe search. Make selection explicit instead of adding a warning.
change: Remove the link warning. Typing filters recipes without changing the current link. Selecting a result changes the recipe. Use name only explicitly selects a custom meal. Save applies the choice.

title: Recipe list
goal: Find a family recipe.
usability: The list is short and clear. The two durations have no visible prep/cook labels. Search can be out of view until the list reveals it.
interaction: Search filters by text. Meal type narrows the list. Plus opens the recipe form.
primary: Search and the recipe title should lead. Keep creation available without dominating the list.
apple: Native searchable lists fit iOS 26. Use the system search presentation in the implementation.
change: Keep search accessible from entry. Label prep and cook times. Expose Recipes at the top of Food.

title: Recipe search: no results
goal: Recover from an unsuccessful search.
usability: The empty-result view explains that the query has no matches.
interaction: The user can edit the query and change the meal filter.
primary: A direct Clear search action reduces the recovery effort.
apple: The native empty view is suitable. Keep query context and a specific recovery action.
change: Add Clear search and explain that the meal filter can also hide matches.

title: Recipe detail, ingredient actions, and method
goal: Read a recipe, prepare ingredients, or start cooking.
usability: Ingredients and method are readable. Cooking uses a flame-only toolbar button; ingredient check and cart actions are close together.
interaction: Each ingredient has separate check and shopping actions. The actions must remain independent.
primary: Start cooking deserves a labelled button near the title and timings.
apple: Native content and toolbar controls suit iOS 26. Keep important actions clear without adding glass to ingredient rows.
change: Add Start cooking near the title. Keep each ingredient’s quantity, check state, and independent add-to-shopping action.

title: Recipe action menu
goal: Edit or delete a recipe.
usability: The ellipsis keeps occasional actions out of the reading flow.
interaction: The menu opens Edit and Delete. Deletion needs a confirmation.
primary: Keep Start cooking outside the secondary action menu.
apple: The native menu is appropriate. Retain clear labels and destructive roles.
change: Keep the menu. Add a prominent Start cooking button on the detail screen.

title: New recipe
goal: Create a recipe with ingredients and steps.
usability: The large empty photo area precedes the required title. It consumes the most valuable space before the user enters any content.
interaction: The form supports ingredient groups, separate steps, a photo, timings, servings, meal type, and a source.
primary: The title and recipe content matter more than an optional photo.
apple: The native form is a good base. Required content should lead the hierarchy.
change: Put Title first. Reduce Photo to an optional row. Keep every content section and its add/remove actions.

title: Edit recipe
goal: Edit the complete recipe without losing content.
usability: The form contains all needed fields. Photo precedes the title. At maximum text size, the ingredient editor shows only part of a line.
interaction: Save applies all sections together. Cancel exits. Existing ingredient groups and steps remain editable.
primary: Title, ingredients, and method need the clearest entry points.
apple: Keep the native form. A consistent field order across create and edit improves predictability.
change: Use the same title-first structure as New recipe. Let ingredient fields expand at large text sizes. Keep the photo, source, groups, and step controls.

title: Cook mode: ingredients
goal: Prepare the ingredients before the first cooking step.
usability: The checklist is useful. The footer calls this page “1 of 5” while the next page says “Step 1 of 4.”
interaction: Checks provide preparation feedback. The next control is an unlabelled visual chevron.
primary: Use Start step 1 and make Ingredients a separate stage from numbered cooking steps.
apple: The full-screen focus and awake display suit cooking. Visible labels improve understanding.
change: Show Before you start, then Start step 1. Count only cooking steps in the step progress.

title: Cook mode: method step
goal: Follow one method step with little effort.
usability: Large step text is useful. The visible “Step 1 of 4” and footer “2 of 5” use different counts.
interaction: Swipe and chevrons move between pages. Previous and Next labels help users with unfamiliar gestures.
primary: Keep the current step and a clear next action prominent.
apple: The focused native screen is appropriate. Keep Reduce Motion support and interruptible system transitions.
change: Use one step count. Add Previous and Next step labels. Keep swipe navigation as an additional path.

title: Cook mode: final step
goal: Finish the recipe and return to its details.
usability: The final Done control is available. In the maximum-text capture, its label wraps inside the footer button and crowds the progress display.
interaction: Done closes cook mode and restores the recipe.
primary: Keep the last instruction visible above Finish cooking.
apple: A native button and predictable return path fit the platform.
change: Use a full-width Finish cooking button and retain Previous step. Keep both labels readable at maximum text size.

title: Shopping list and low-stock suggestions
goal: Add and purchase shopping items.
usability: The list supports a fast shopping task. Inventory is below the shopping content, so a long list can hide it.
interaction: The check control purchases an item. The item menu supports rename and delete.
primary: Adding an item and marking a purchase should remain the fastest actions.
apple: The native list and floating tab bar fit iOS 26. Separate shopping from stock actions clearly.
change: Use the chosen Household overview with Shopping list and Inventory navigation rows, followed by low-stock items. Keep inline rename and five-second purchase Undo in Shopping list.

title: Shopping item menu
goal: Rename or delete one shopping item.
usability: The item menu is compact and appropriate for occasional actions.
interaction: The menu opens a rename sheet or a delete confirmation.
primary: Keep purchase outside the menu as the direct check action.
apple: The native menu fits the platform.
change: Rename activates an inline field in the existing row. Delete keeps its confirmation. Keep purchase as a separate check action.

title: Rename shopping item
goal: Correct a shopping item name.
usability: The current sheet takes the user away from the shopping list for a single-field edit.
interaction: Save applies the name. Cancel returns without changes.
primary: Keep the item in its original row. Focus the name field and provide a clear commit and cancel action.
apple: Use native text entry and keyboard support within the row.
change: Replace the rename sheet with inline text entry. Done saves a non-empty name. Cancel keeps the original name. Keep failed edits in place with an error.

title: Purchase feedback and Undo
goal: Mark an item purchased and correct an accidental check.
usability: Purchased items remain visible and can be restored. This supports correction.
interaction: Clear purchased items asks for confirmation. A linked purchase can also need a stock update.
primary: The user wants checked items hidden after five seconds. Keep Undo visible during that interval.
apple: The native list and confirmation are suitable. Text must explain status independently of color.
change: Remove the Purchased section and its clear action. Keep the checked row in place with Undo for five seconds, then hide it. Undo restores the unchecked state.

title: Restock after purchase
goal: Update inventory after purchasing a linked item.
usability: The form already shows current stock and offers Not now. The transition from purchase to stock entry needs a short explanation.
interaction: The user enters a quantity or percentage and confirms Restock.
primary: Show the current level, the new level, and an explicit defer action.
apple: The native sheet is appropriate. Keep the two decisions clear and recoverable.
change: Keep stock updates optional through Inventory. Do not interrupt a shopping check with this form. Retain the current stock, a cancel action, and the new-level label.

title: Inventory overview
goal: Find an area and see stock that needs attention.
usability: The six-item Running Low list comes before Areas. It pushes the main navigation toward or below the bottom edge.
interaction: Area rows open their contents. Low-stock rows can add one item to Shopping.
primary: Area navigation needs a stable, visible position.
apple: Native lists work well. Content order should support navigation before a long status list.
change: Place Areas first and Running low below. Keep every low-stock item and its shopping action.

title: Inventory area
goal: Read stock levels and adjust household items.
usability: Counts, level bars, low-stock status, and cart controls share each row. Some row-wide edit actions lack a clear visual cue.
interaction: Tap the item name to edit. Plus/minus adjusts count. Cart adds the item to Shopping.
primary: Keep quick stock adjustments separate from row navigation and shopping.
apple: Native list rows are suitable. Clear control boundaries and target sizes matter more than decoration.
change: Use a clear edit affordance, explicit stock values, and distinct shopping controls. Retain All and Running low filters.

title: Inventory area menu
goal: Edit or delete an inventory area.
usability: The long-press menu is useful as a shortcut but is hard to discover as the only visible edit route.
interaction: Long press or swipe reveals Edit and Delete. Deletion also removes the area’s items.
primary: A visible area action menu helps users find edit and delete.
apple: Native context menus suit shortcuts. Important management actions need a discoverable alternative.
change: Add a visible area action menu. Keep long press and swipe as shortcuts.

title: New inventory area
goal: Name a storage area and select its icon and colour.
usability: The compact form and preview explain the result well.
interaction: Name receives keyboard focus. Save stays disabled until the name has text.
primary: Name, Save, and the preview are available.
apple: This is a suitable native form. Avoid a broad redesign.
change: Keep the form. Add one short description of what an area represents.

title: Edit inventory area
goal: Change an area name, icon, or colour.
usability: The form matches area creation and includes a preview.
interaction: Save applies the area changes. Cancel returns to Inventory.
primary: Keep the current values and preview visible.
apple: The consistent native form follows platform conventions.
change: Retain this form and use the same field order as New area.

title: New inventory item: count
goal: Add an item with a count and low-stock threshold.
usability: The form is short. Count and Level are domain terms that benefit from a household example.
interaction: The tracking choice changes the stock controls. Save needs a name.
primary: Name, quantity, unit, and the meaning of the threshold need clear labels.
apple: Native form controls suit this task. A numeric field can complement a stepper for large counts.
change: Explain Count and Level. Label the threshold explicitly and retain precise numeric input.

title: Edit inventory item: level
goal: Update a partly used item and its low-stock threshold.
usability: The percentage and slider express current stock. The form says “Low below,” but the iOS model includes the threshold value in its low-stock state.
interaction: The slider updates the remaining level. Save applies the form; Delete asks for confirmation.
primary: Keep the current percentage and threshold together.
apple: Native slider and form controls fit iOS. Add a precise numeric entry route if the slider alone is too coarse.
change: Use Remaining level and Alert at or below. Keep the percentage, slider, Save, and delete confirmation.

title: Settings and profile
goal: Manage this iPhone, the profile, and family settings.
usability: The list groups App and Admin. The avatar label says Open profile, but the destination says Settings. At maximum text size, identity and photo controls delay the settings list.
interaction: Done closes the sheet. Links open settings details. Admin-only entries depend on the current role.
primary: Users need a clear distinction between this iPhone and changes that affect the whole family.
apple: Native inset-grouped settings and sheets suit iOS 26. Name the entry and destination consistently.
change: Use Settings for the entry label. Separate This iPhone and Family administration. Retain every existing settings destination.

title: System photo picker
goal: Choose a profile photo.
usability: The app uses the system picker. The capture shows its loading state; the settled photo gallery is not reviewed.
interaction: Selection returns an image to the app. Cancel leaves the profile unchanged.
primary: Keep photo selection inside the system picker and show upload feedback in Settings.
apple: Retain the native Photos picker. Do not reproduce its interface with a custom design.
change: No picker redesign. Preserve upload feedback and retry errors in the profile.

title: Server configuration
goal: Change the server connection for this iPhone.
usability: The form is compact. Connect can sign the user out. The captured accessibility hierarchy exposes an unnamed Server URL button when the demo URL is empty.
interaction: Connect validates and discovers server settings before saving. Cancel exits.
primary: Explain the sign-out effect before submission and preserve the current configuration on failure.
apple: The native form fits iOS. Important consequences need plain text near the action.
change: State that connecting to another server signs the user out. Keep the address and error inline.

title: Chore reminders and device permission
goal: Enable this iPhone’s notifications and set the family reminder schedule.
usability: The screen combines a local permission with a family-wide schedule. Disabled demo controls need a visible reason.
interaction: The device control opens or changes local permission. Admins edit both shared times and save.
primary: Separate the local permission state from the family schedule and show the time zone.
apple: Native toggles and time pickers are suitable. Use labels and explanatory text for disabled states.
change: Group This iPhone and Family reminder schedule. Explain demo limitations and unavailable server push support.

title: Family broadcast: compose
goal: Send a short message to family iPhones.
usability: The form has a message field, character count, and Send. The text already explains lock-screen exposure.
interaction: Send stays disabled for invalid text or unavailable push support. The keyboard has Done.
primary: Use a household label such as Family message. Explain that only registered iPhones receive it.
apple: The native form works. Keep the action label and delivery scope understandable.
change: Rename the screen Family message. Keep the 500-character limit and lock-screen explanation. Preserve the message after a failed send.

title: Family broadcast: result
goal: Understand whether the family message reaches any registered devices.
usability: “Apple accepted: 0” is transport language. At maximum text size, the result sits below the message field and can remain outside the viewport.
interaction: The result remains in the form. Retry must not repeat accepted notifications.
primary: Lead with the outcome and next step. Apple acceptance does not prove device display or reading.
apple: Clear human feedback is more important than transport detail in a household app.
change: Lead with No available iPhones for the zero-device case. Move focus to the result. Retain the message and link to notification setup.

title: Home information and location
goal: Set the home location and arrival margin.
usability: Coordinates and the time zone are present. “Home Info” does not explain weather and departures.
interaction: The user captures device location, confirms it, then saves. This avoids silently changing the home location.
primary: Explain the purpose and preserve the explicit location confirmation.
apple: Native location permission and form controls are suitable. Technical coordinates need plain context.
change: Use Home location. Explain weather, departures, and arrival margin. Keep coordinates available and keep confirm-before-save.

title: Family name
goal: Change the name shown to the family.
usability: The one-field form and family-wide explanation are sufficient.
interaction: Save applies the name and returns. Empty text disables Save.
primary: The field needs a label that remains visible after entry.
apple: Keep the native form. No structural redesign is needed.
change: Add a persistent Family name label. Retain the explanation and Save behavior.

title: Family members and role actions
goal: See family membership and manage roles.
usability: Names, emails, and the Admin badge are clear. Promote and Demote only appear after a swipe.
interaction: A swipe changes another member’s role. The current user has no self-demote action.
primary: Role changes need a discoverable path and a plain explanation of the permission effect.
apple: Native rows are suitable. Swipe-only role management is hard to discover.
change: Open role details from the member row. Explain Member and Admin. Confirm a change and retain the self-protection rule.

title: Category list and actions
goal: Create and manage chore categories.
usability: The list is short and easy to scan. Main Course and Salads look like recipe categories in the demo, which confuses the chore purpose.
interaction: Plus creates a category. Swipe exposes rename and delete.
primary: Explain what categories organise and make editing discoverable.
apple: Native lists, sheets, and confirmations are suitable.
change: Keep the native list. Add a chore-focused explanation and a visible row action. Correct the demo category examples.

title: New category
goal: Create a named chore category.
usability: The short name sheet matches the task.
interaction: Save applies a valid name. Cancel returns without changes.
primary: A category name and visible Save are sufficient.
apple: Retain the native form and standard sheet controls.
change: Keep the form. Use a persistent Category name label.

title: Rename category
goal: Rename an existing category.
usability: The short sheet suits the task. A family-wide effect explanation can prevent surprises.
interaction: Save applies the name. Delete remains a separate confirmed action.
primary: Keep the current name visible and editable.
apple: Retain the native sheet and text field.
change: Add a short family-wide effect explanation. Keep deletion separate.

title: API token list and empty state
goal: Manage credentials used by other apps.
usability: The empty state offers a plus-based next step but does not explain why a family admin needs a token.
interaction: Plus opens a name sheet. Existing tokens can be deleted.
primary: Explain the purpose and the effect of deletion before creation.
apple: Native list and empty-state controls are suitable.
change: Explain that tokens connect other apps and act like passwords. Keep the token list in family administration.

title: Create API token
goal: Create a token with an identifiable name.
usability: The name-only sheet is concise. It does not explain the one-time reveal before creation.
interaction: Save creates the token and opens its one-time value.
primary: Use Create token and explain the next step.
apple: Native sheet controls fit the task. Action-specific wording improves feedback.
change: Use a clear token name label, Create token, and a one-time reveal notice.

title: Token created and copied
goal: Copy the newly created token before dismissing it.
usability: The existing screen already warns that the token appears once. This is useful.
interaction: Copy Token copies the value. Done closes the reveal. The capture does not show a distinct copied confirmation.
primary: Keep the copy action and one-time warning above other content.
apple: Native selectable text and copy controls are suitable. Confirm completion with text.
change: Retain the one-time reveal. Change the copy label briefly to Copied and announce the result.

title: Calendar display menu
goal: Choose the calendar display.
usability: The menu contains four supported modes. Its icon does not reveal the active mode before the menu opens.
interaction: The native menu selects Year, Month, Week, or Day.
primary: Show the active mode and keep Today available.
apple: Keep a native menu or segmented control. Avoid a custom glass panel.
change: Keep the current Calendar design and interactions, as selected by the user. Only remove arrival-margin text. Earlier layout proposals are superseded.

title: Chore recurrence variants
goal: Set monthly or custom repeat rules and stop conditions.
usability: These variants add a day of month, interval unit, end date, or task limit. The form needs a readable summary as options change.
interaction: Native pickers and switches reveal the relevant controls. Both stop conditions remain available.
primary: Show the resulting schedule before Save.
apple: Native form controls are appropriate. Keep custom weekday targets large and label each option plainly.
change: Retain all recurrence variants. Add a schedule summary and plain labels.

title: Edit inventory item: count
goal: Change an item quantity, unit, or threshold.
usability: The stock values are explicit. Large quantities need more than repeated stepper taps.
interaction: The stepper changes quantity and threshold. Save applies the values.
primary: Keep the quantity and unit together. Offer direct numeric entry.
apple: Native numeric entry and steppers fit the platform.
change: Keep the stepper and add precise numeric entry. Retain unit and threshold.

title: Inventory area: empty
goal: Start stock records in a new area.
usability: The empty area keeps its filter and an Add Item action.
interaction: Add Item opens the same item form used in populated areas.
primary: The next action is to add the first item.
apple: Keep the native empty explanation and navigation.
change: Use a clear empty-state message and retain Add item. No broader redesign is needed.
